intro: An Australian singer of 1920s hokum and calypso.
story: C.W. Stoneking was born on March 15, 1974, in Katherine, Northern Territory, and plays old-style country blues on National guitar and tenor banjo. Jungle Blues won the ARIA for Best Blues and Roots Album in 2009, the year of his first Pickathon, and Gon' Boogaloo, which swapped the National for an electric Jazzmaster, won the same category in 2015. It reached the U.S. in June 2016, and NPR caught him on his first American tour that year. He returned to the farm in 2016, and in 2026 finished a 23-date European tour.
artist_reel_line: Gon' Boogaloo won the 2015 ARIA for Best Blues and Roots Album.

intro: A Portland old-time band, here for the eighth time.
story: Caleb Klauder and Sammy Lind began Foghorn Stringband around 2000 in Portland, and Reeb Willms moved to Portland and joined in 2011. Outshine the Sun, recorded in a Portland living room, came out in 2012, and Willamette Week called them the flagship band of the city's old-time revival. They played Pickathon in 2002, 2003, 2005, 2009, 2010, 2012, 2013 and 2016, and by December 2024 were nearing 25 years together.

intro: Three Oregon sisters with blood harmonies.
story: Joseph began as a Portland trio of Natalie Closner and the twins Allison and Meegan; Natalie, a solo songwriter, recruited the twins, and the name honors their grandfather and his hometown of Joseph, Oregon. Native Dreamer Kin came out in early 2014, and I'm Alone, No You're Not on ATO on August 26, 2016, produced by Mike Mogis; NPR's First Listen said sweetness and power aren't mutually exclusive on it. Meegan said she wrote the title phrase in her journal, and fans have tattooed it, one half on each wrist. They played Pickathon in 2015 and 2016. Natalie and Meegan later carried on as a duo with Closer to Happy.

intro: A songwriter stepping into his own, back for a second year.
story: Kevin Morby left New York in 2013 after years as a Woods bassist and a co-founder of The Babies, and settled in Los Angeles's Mount Washington neighborhood. Singing Saw, his third solo album and first for Dead Oceans, came out on April 15, 2016, produced by Sam Cohen at Isokon Studios in Woodstock, and NPR said he sounds like he has had experience for a lifetime of records. He played Pickathon in 2015 and 2016. City Music followed in 2017, Oh My God in 2019 and Sundowner in 2020, and Little Wide Open, produced by Aaron Dessner, in 2026.

King Sunny Adé was born Sunday Adeniyi Adegeye in 1946, and the press crowned him King of Juju in 1977 after hit albums with his band the African Beats. He signed to Island Records in 1982, and Juju Music and Synchro System brought juju to international audiences; Synchro System earned a 1983 Grammy nomination, the first for a Nigerian artist, and Odu was nominated for Best World Music Album. He played Pickathon in 2016. He turned 80 in 2026, more than 60 years into his career, and chairs Nigeria's Musical Copyright Society.
artist_reel_line: He turned 80 in 2026 with more than 60 years in music.

intro: A Sun City Girls guitarist of global improvisation.
story: Sir Richard Bishop founded the experimental band Sun City Girls in Phoenix with his brother Alan and the drummer Charles Gocher. His first solo album, Salvador Kali, came out in 1998 on John Fahey's Revenant label, and for Drag City he made Polytheistic Fragments, The Freak of Araby and Tangier Sessions in 2015. Sun City Girls ended in 2007, and he took up solo touring. He played Pickathon in 2016. Oneiric Formulary followed on Drag City in 2020 and Hillbilly Ragas in 2025, and in October 2026 he toured Australia.

Luke and Tess Pretty formed Tennyson in Edmonton, Alberta, in 2012 after busking as kids, Luke on electronic production and Tess on drums. They played Pickathon in 2016. Luke released his full-length debut, Rot, on Counter Records on February 18, 2022, and in 2026 the EP plx and the single You Want My Everything.

Emmett Kelly, born in Los Angeles and long based in Chicago, plays in Bonnie "Prince" Billy's backing band and leads The Cairo Gang. Goes Missing came out on Drag City's God? imprint on June 23, 2015, written and recorded largely on the road, often in his van, and Paste said he now stakes his own claim after backing Will Oldham. They played Pickathon in 2016. Untouchable followed on Drag City in 2017, and in 2024 Kelly joined Stephen Malkmus, Matt Sweeney and Jim White in the supergroup Hard Quartet.
